description: VF4 plan mutability + no server-side concurrency control, as an ILLUSTRATIVE request/response sequence that encodes the STATICALLY-INFERRED contract from the GW ConfigurationDomainLogicV1.ValidateAsync controller (see source-extracts/ConfigurationDomainLogicV1.cs). This is a hand-authored representative sequence, NOT an observed runtime capture. The STATIC evidence (authenticated in provenance.test.ts against the extracts) is: the controller reads no precondition and dispatches the validation command unconditionally, the store upserts validations/latest with no version/precondition parameter, the exception mapper maps no 412, and ValidationProperties.g.cs declares no eTag/version/concurrency wire field. From that, the inferred contract is: two successive validations of the SAME configuration resolve to the SAME singleton (.../configurations/cfg-demo/validations/latest); a client that attempts an If-Match precondition on the second validate sends a CONCRETE NONMATCHING ETag — a value a precondition-HONORING service would reject with 412 Precondition Failed — yet the inferred contract accepts it with the normal external 202 (never a 412), returns no ETag, and validations/latest is REPLACED in place (plan A -> plan B). Using a nonmatching ETag (rather than a match-any `*`, which any resource satisfies) is what makes the illustration meaningful: only a service that IGNORES the precondition returns 202 here. ARM exposes no eTag, If-Match/If-None-Match precondition, idempotency key, or version guard on validations/latest, so nothing prevents a later validation from replacing the current execution plan between an execute's validate and execute calls.

sequence.note: First validate action is accepted; validations/latest will hold plan A.
GET validations/latest is terminal-success and holds plan A.

A LATER validate action attempts an If-Match precondition with a CONCRETE NONMATCHING ETag — a value a precondition-HONORING service would reject with 412. The statically-inferred contract IGNORES it: accepted with the normal 202 (NOT a 412), carries no ETag, and replaces validations/latest in place. (Illustrative of the statically-inferred contract, not an observed capture.)
GET validations/latest now holds a DIFFERENT plan B on the SAME resource id: the If-Match did not prevent replacement and no version bump exists the client could have pinned.
